findings.evidence: Step 2.7's purpose paragraph spends 9 lines explaining why an absent `purpose` is a legacy-compat default ("an assumption that must be a deliberate, documented legacy-compat default, never an accident..."). Step 3 (lines 368-380) repeats the same rationale, and Step 2.6 (lines 276-285) spends 10 lines saying `strength` is unused.
findings.fix: Shorten each to one rule plus a one-clause reason ("Ask purpose review/execute/both; a new entry never leaves it unset because absent means both"). Delete the repeat in Step 3 and keep Step 2.6 to two lines.

findings.evidence: "This skill is a **Process** (a fixed Step 0→4 sequence...)" runs to 468 lines, more than twice the ~200-line Process pattern. Long prose rationale blocks hide the checkpoints.
findings.fix: Add a short progress checklist (Step 0 locate, 1 detect plus check-providers, 2.1 target plus announce, 2.2-2.8 asks, 3 render-toml, 4 exit-status/warnings/trust). Move the rationale prose into a reference so the main body reads as a phased workflow with checkpoints.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list is strong, but environment gotchas are scattered through the steps and not collected: the trust-local --cwd `.aikit/` pitfall (line 449), the nested `extra = {timeout_tiers}` silent fallback (line 360), and the diff-not-cmp trailing newline (line 404).
findings.fix: Add a short `## Gotchas` section next to NEVER that lists these environment facts, each with its consequence (exits 1, silently falls back to the policy default, a false mismatch).

findings.evidence: The description gives WHAT, WHEN and flags but no boundary against its near-miss sibling ai-kit-spec-review (running the review itself). It also lacks intent phrasings such as reviewer ladder, fallback order or a stale opencode provider.
findings.fix: Set up or refresh cross-AI reviewer config: detect installed CLIs (codex, cursor, opencode, pi, claude, grok) and their models, ask which to use and in what priority/fallback order, test each pair, then write review-spec.toml (default ./.aikit/review-spec.toml, path always announced; asks before replacing any existing local or global file). Use when the user wants to configure, add, reorder or check cross-AI reviewers or executors, fix a reviewer ladder, check stale opencode providers in review-spec, or when ai-kit-spec-review warns no config exists, even without naming review-spec.toml. Flags: --check-only (report availability and quota, no writes), --local, --global (~/.config/ai-kit/review-spec.toml). Not for running a cross-AI review or executing a plan (ai-kit-spec-review / ai-kit-cross-ai).

findings.evidence: The SKILL.md body is 468 lines of dense prose (about 7000 tokens, above the ~5000 recommendation). Steps 2.4 (codex/cursor/grok command details), 2.8 (timeout_tiers) and 4 (trust-local JSON shape) run on every run, even when the user picks no codex, no cursor or a global target.
findings.fix: Move the runtime-specific detail in Step 2.4 (codex bare-id, cursor build-model-id, grok/custom command grammar) into a reference loaded only when that runtime is selected. Move the trust-local detail into one loaded only when the target is local. Keep a one-line rule plus a read-trigger in the main body.

findings.evidence: "is this CLI's quota reliable enough to be a primary pick... does this model's strength... actually match" is judgment guidance with no default ladder shape. This is the one high-freedom area in an otherwise precisely calibrated skill.
findings.fix: Give a default (for example: external flagship pairs first by purpose-weighted rank, free-tier or tight-quota CLIs after them, the session default last) and keep reordering as the escape hatch.

findings.evidence: Five of the six evals assert check-providers behaviour. No assertion covers the core contract: the local default plus "Writing to:" announced before the questions, an explicit purpose on every new entry, "(running under: unknown)", the codex bare model id, the render-toml exit/WARNING handling, or trust-local --show before trusting. Only one eval has an input file.
findings.fix: Add evals with fixtures for: an unknown host session-default ask (assert the literal "(running under: unknown)" and model = ""), a codex high-effort pick (assert model = "gpt-5.6-sol" and effort = "high"), a render-toml WARNING stderr fixture (assert no plain success report), and a local write (assert trust-local --cwd <root> --show runs before any trust).

findings.evidence: 16 queries (8/8), but the negatives are mostly unrelated ("Explain how git rebase differs from git merge", "Refactor the Cursor status line module"). There is no near-miss such as running a cross-AI review, executing a plan through cross-AI, or editing opencode.jsonc providers.
findings.fix: Grow to about 20 queries and replace three or four easy negatives with near-misses: "run a cross-AI review of PLAN.md with codex", "execute this plan with the cheap cross-AI executor", "add a new provider to my opencode.jsonc", "why did my cross-AI review time out". Add one or two casual or typo'd positives that never name review-spec.

findings.evidence: "Also `is_router`/`fallback_quota` when Step 2.2/2.7 confirmed either as `true`". Step 2.7 never asks about is_router or fallback_quota, so for a session-default entry this branch has no input to act on.
findings.fix: Either add the is_router/fallback_quota question to Step 2.7 or change the line to "when Step 2.2 (cli-model-selection.md) confirmed either as true; session-default entries never carry them".

findings.evidence: "Outside `--check-only`, when `probe-quota` prints `ignoring untrusted project-local config`...". The normal Step 0-4 flow never runs probe-quota, so the agent cannot tell when this branch applies.
findings.fix: State the trigger explicitly (for example "If you or ai-kit-spec-review later run probe-quota in this project and it prints..."), or move the sentence to check-only.md / the ai-kit-spec-review skill, where probe-quota actually runs.
